The patient usually presents with one or both thumbs locked in flexion at the IP joint (Figure 1). in_text_mentions: High-resolution US revealed a hyperechoic calcific deposit within the superficial layer of the A1 pulley (Figures 2A, 2B), clearly distinguishable from the underlying flexor tendon and adjacent sesamoid bone (Figure 3A). Power Doppler imaging showed mild hyperemia in the surrounding soft tissue, supporting the presence of active inflammation (Figure 3B). No significant tendon nodule or additional pulley thickening was observed.
